column5: Sunlight init: sets ShadeStart/ShadeRange/Inclination (0x937aae/0x937aaf/0x937ab0) to the exe defaults 0x1c/0xf/0x20, and sunX/sunZ/sunBase (0x937aa8/0x937aaa/0x937aac) to the literal immediate **0x93 (147)**, all three - not derived from ShadeStart/ShadeRange/Inclination at all, a flat hardcoded constant - then calls sunlight_init_2 (0x401790). Live-measured this session on two running levels with different on-disk Inclination (0x40/0x20): sunX=sunZ=sunBase=147 in both, turn 20 and turn 77 (9+ multiples of the 8-turn tick 0x401350 checks), confirming the level's own sunlight block never visibly moves the vector away from this flat default in normal play - see 0x401350/0x401920/0x4be230 - pop3-rev-analysis.md "Terrain land colour"

Near-duplicate of part of sunlight_init_default: sets sunX/sunZ/sunBase to the same flat 0x93 (147) without touching ShadeStart/ShadeRange/Inclination, then falls through into sunlight_init_2 (0x401790) - a "reset the light vector to flat" helper reused from more than one call site
`sunlight_update_unit_landscape`: a dynamic ground light following a unit (50 at most)

Per-turn sun-angle tick, gated: no-op unless flag bit 0x895da5&0x8 is set (live-measured this session: it isn't, in normal single-level play - Inclination stayed at its on-disk value across 9+ ticks, see 0x401040); when set and the turn counter's low 3 bits are all 1 (every 8th turn), increments Inclination (0x937ab0) by 1 and recomputes sunX/sunBase (0x937aa8/0x937aac) from REAL sin/cos tables indexed by the new Inclination (0x5de5e8/0x5ddde8, scaled), then calls sunlight_init_2 (0x401790) - this, not the level's static sunlight block, is the exe's actual day/night-style sun-angle animation mechanism, and it appears disabled in the sessions measured this session

Builds two unrelated 1024-entry angle-keyed shade tables (0x89bc8e, 0x89c08d) from the sin/cos tables (0x5ddde8/0x5de5e8) dotted against the sun vector (0x937aa8/0x937aaa/0x937aac) and ShadeStart/ShadeRange (0x937aae/0x937aaf); does not itself write the sun vector, only reads it - role of the two output tables not traced further this session

Unconditionally forces Inclination (0x937ab0) to 0x40 (64, overwriting whatever the level set) and sunX/sunBase (0x937aa8/0x937aac) from two FIXED scalar memory cells, 0x5de9e8/0x5de1e8 - NOT an array indexed by Inclination (no writes to either address found anywhere in the exe's code this session, so they are build-time data constants, not computed from the level's sunlight block) - then calls sunlight_init_2 (0x401790); gated behind flag bit 0x895da5&0x8 like 0x401350, same early-return. Despite the name "Inclination=64 init path" this is not a per-Inclination branch - it hardcodes a SINGLE fixed result whenever it runs

`fn(thing, new_state)` - the generic class-agnostic "set per-turn state" helper used throughout the exe (effects, scenery, etc. all call this or inline the same 3-step idiom: `0x4ed6f0` leave-state hook, write `+0x2c`, `0x4ed640` enter-state hook). **Key finding this session**: if flag `thing+0xe` bit 0x10 is SET, this function does NOTHING AT ALL - not even writing the state byte. Confirmed (via the Reincarnation Centre intro investigation) to mean "this object's state is externally/scripted-controlled, don't let generic per-type init code touch it" - `0x4a7d80`'s own row (reincarnation pillar init) and `0x50c780`'s own row (`prepare rs land`) both inline-check the same bit before their own state-setup block for exactly this reason.

Generic "set this thing's state" helper, called as fn(thing, new_state): unless thing+0xe bit 0x10 is set, calls 0x4ed6f0(thing) (removes it from its current state's processing list), writes new_state to thing+0x2c, then calls 0x4ed640(thing) (re-adds it to the new state's list) - used across many classes, not just effects (e.g. 0x445bbb sets a person's state after assigning tribe/type fields); corrects the previous draft of this row, which wrongly described this as an effect-specific dispatcher reading table 0x50afd4 - that dispatch actually lives in a separate function, see 0x50a750

`fn(self, pos_struct*)`, called from state 23's roll-failure sub-state 6 (0x4D8CC4, see 0x4D83B0) right after a cell-lookup (0x405050) and a call to 0x4044B0 on the candidate's OWN resolved cell+0x8 building occupant (see that row's correction, 2026-10-29: 0x4044B0 is a building door-point calc, not a "cell-link" - this row's old "cell-link call" wording was a guess, not confirmed) - plausibly finalises the unit's cell/placement bookkeeping for a new position; not independently traced this session.

Class-2 (building) per-state ENTER dispatch (same one-time-on-transition convention already confirmed for class 1/`init_unit_class_1` and class 10/`init_unit_class_10`), switch at `0x403264`, states 1-6 (`cl=[esi+0x2c]-1`). State 4 (burning, "Burning building" pop3-rev-analysis.md) -> `0x408840` (own row). States 1/2/3/5/6 not individually traced this session (addresses `0x4030EC`/`0x40318A`/`0x403195`/`0x4031AD`/`0x4031C2`).

The generic per-turn BUILDING (class 2) dispatcher, confirmed this session as the class-2 case of the universal `unit_processing_class_N` table (`0x4ED7EC`). Found/traced this session (task #12, chasing `0x4B8BB0`'s own "owner state==4" gate) a state TRANSITION INTO building state 4: when a per-type flag (table `0x5A7272`, bit `0x1`) is CLEAR, a flag bit (`+0xC` bit `0x100000`) is set, and the building isn't already in state 4, it stops its current state (`0x4ED6F0`), sets `+0x2C=4`, restarts it (`0x4ED640`), and preserves the per-instance damage/scorch marker (`+0xAF`, the SAME field `0x4BA2C0` clears on repair) across the transition - consistent with state 4 being a "damaged, awaiting repair" state, though the exact trigger (what sets that `+0xC` bit `0x100000` flag in the first place) was not traced this session. Also calls the building-placement-preamble functions `0x403D50`/`0x403A00`/`0x403F00` (all own rows) once per turn under an `+0xC` bit `0x8000000` one-shot flag (a deferred "just moved/placed, redo my footprint" step), and a large amount of further per-turn upkeep (walls, worship/mana fields `+0x9C`/`+0xA7`/`+0xAD`/`+0xAE`, etc.) not read this session. Only the state-4 transition and the deferred-footprint-redo were traced; the bulk of this dispatcher's own body (several hundred bytes past `0x4033A3`) is unread.

The ordinary class-2 (building) per-turn function (already named in pop3-rev-analysis.md's Reference, no row of its own until now). General per-turn bookkeeping (shake-jitter decay, `0x408080` foundation check call, timers) then, for state 2 ("operational") buildings, a jump table (`switchD_00403536`, Ghidra-named cases 2-6, keyed on `state-2`) by the building's own class-2 STATE (not type): state 2 itself further splits by a per-type table byte (`0x5A7228`+0x48, bits `0x20`/`0x1`/`0x40`) into one of three per-type operational handlers - bit `0x1` -> `0x405B80` (`training_building_turn`, already traced), bit `0x40` -> `0x406600` (own row, vehicle-hut production - the four vehicle-hut types 13-16 are confirmed to set exactly this bit), bit `0x20` -> `0x4055F0` (not traced this session, by elimination the likely hut-breeding/growth per-turn hook). State 3 -> `0x406F40` (destroy/finalize), state 4 -> `0x408AB0`, state 5 -> `0x407060`, state 6 -> `0x4F1530` (none of 3/4/5/6 individually traced this session).

Writes the per-cell map table's (0x8a03e4) +0xe LOW nibble (shared byte with the high-nibble "downhill direction" level_land_processing_2 0x44df40 writes) via calc_unit_shade_value (0x450d50): `cl = cell[+0xe]; cl = (cl & 0xf0) | clamp(calc_unit_shade_value(cell), 0, 0xf); cell[+0xe] = cl` - preserves the downhill nibble, replaces only this one. Gated on a per-call flag (`[edi]` bit 0x1, edi from a per-thing/shape lookup via table 0x895ec1 using the caller's own thing record fields +0x26/+0x33/+0x7a/+0x7c) and only runs for the cell(s) under the caller's own footprint (`esp+0x10` packed x/z, same `(x&0xfe)*2|(z&0xfe00)` addressing as compute_cell_light 0x4be230). Called from 5 sites exe-wide (0x4032bc, 0x4036e1, 0x4038c6, 0x4038d1, 0x404be6, 0x4ba37d) - not yet traced individually, but given the sibling `landscape_set_unit_shadow`'s own call sites (building-placement-era code, see below), this is almost certainly "recompute this object's ground-shadow footprint whenever it moves/changes," i.e. the per-cell "ambient_nibble" compute_cell_light (0x4be230) reads is really an **object/building shadow intensity**, not a static light constant - resolves the contradiction between a live measurement (nonzero +0xe low nibble under a hill's temple) and pop3-rev-analysis.md's prior "nothing writes it, probably always 0" conclusion, which only looked at terrain-specific functions and missed this unit-movement-triggered writer - pop3-rev-analysis.md "Terrain land colour"

Same per-cell +0xe low-nibble write as landscape_move_1 (0x403a00, byte-for-byte identical RMW: `cl=(cell[+0xe]&0xf0)|clamp(calc_unit_shade_value(cell),0,0xf)`), minus that function's thing-lookup/gating preamble - takes the record pointer more directly. Called from 3 sites in the 0x4a6000-0x4a7000 range (0x4a68b6, 0x4a6f25, 0x4a7e82, not individually traced this session but that address range is building/object-placement code elsewhere in this catalog), consistent with "(re)apply an object's ground shadow when it's placed/moved" - pop3-rev-analysis.md "Terrain land colour"

Found this session tracing `init_unit_building`'s (0x4036D0) preamble (its very first call). Computes the ground HEIGHT at a newly-placed building's own door point: resolves its shape/door-offset via the shape table (0x895ec1, indexed by the building's own shape id `+0x33`) and a 4-way facing switch (quantized from `+0x26`) to pick a rotated door-adjacent corner offset from the shared shape-data table (`0x59df3c+0x2c`, same table `landscape_set_unit_shadow`/0x403c10 and 0x403f00 below read for their own footprint walks), adds the building's own door-offset fields (`+0x7a`/`+0x7c`), clamps the result on-map (0x4ee580), samples ground height there via the universal terrain-height function (0x44e940, same one `compute_cell_light`'s docs already cite for `ground()`), and stores it into the building's own `+0x41` height field, clearing flag `+0x10` bit `0x400`. Not the same function as 0x4044b0 ("a building's door point", below) - this one goes one step further to also sample height, and was not checked this session for whether it literally calls 0x4044b0 internally or duplicates its math. Called from `init_unit_building` (0x4036D1) before the footprint shadow recompute (`landscape_move_1`, 0x403a00) - pop3-rev-analysis.md has no "building placement" write-up yet to attach this to.

Found this session, same `init_unit_building` (0x4036D0) preamble, called next (0x4036F0) for every building type EXCEPT 0xa (wall, `cmp [esi+0x2b],0xa`). Ground-flattening under a newly-placed building's footprint: walks the building's own footprint cells (same shape table 0x895ec1/0x59df3c as 0x403d50/0x403c10 above), reads each footprint cell's own HEIGHT field (table 0x8a03e4 `+0x4` - not the shadow nibble `+0xe`) plus its neighbours, accumulates and divides by the sample count to get one flat target height, then writes that averaged height back into `+0x4` for 4 cells around each footprint corner - levelling the ground to one flat plane under the whole building. A type-indexed table (`0x5a7270`, bits `0x20000`/`0x40000`) adjusts the minimum averaging sample count per building type first. For types `0xd`/`0xe` specifically (boat huts, per `docs/unit_types`) a further gated 4-way jump table overrides 3 of the same 4 corner cells' `+0x4` height with the just-computed average offset by -1 on some corners - plausibly carving a one-step-lower boat ramp into the flattened pad; not live-confirmed. This is the actual terrain-flattening step of building placement - pop3-rev-analysis.md's building/construction write-up doesn't cite an address for this yet.

`fn(unit, &out_pos) -> void` - despite Ghidra's "get_building_coords" name (wrong, corrects it: works on any class-1/mesh-bearing unit, not buildings specifically), computes the world-space attachment anchor for whatever 3D prop/mesh is currently attached to `unit` (its own `+0x33` mesh index into the `objs0_struct` table, `0x895EC1`, field `+0x2c`, combined with the unit's own facing `+0x26` and a secondary per-mesh anchor-offset table at `0x59DF3C`) and writes the resulting {x,z} into `*out_pos`; reads the unit's own `+0x7a`/`+0x7c` as the reference position to offset from. Found tracing preach_order_handler's (`0x43C7A0`) calls while chasing "does the preacher's own gesture come from a pose table" (it doesn't - see that row); this and its sibling `0x40A980` (below) are the geometry support for attaching a prop mesh via `0x4F14B0`, not animation-pose selectors themselves.
a building's door point (pos, shape origin, door offset)
hut completion: `grow = 0`, `breed = target - 54`
hut breeding, every 4 turns; spawns the brave at 0x404E2C

get_cell(pos*): rounds the given x/z position down to even cells and returns a pointer into the per-cell record table at 0x8a03e4 for that cell; +0xc of the returned record holds a terrain-type nibble read by 0x4d66e0/0x4d4a00/order-kind-3 (0x4336c0) via the 0x5aa328 terrain-flags table.

Pre-existing row said "hut growth, every 16 turns; creates the next size at 0x4051FE" - **extended this session (task #12), chasing `0x4BA2C0`'s own "normal construction, positive delta, caller not found" open question, which this partially resolves.** `fn(building) -> bool`: gated on a per-type "can this type even exist/grow" table (`0x5A725C`, type-indexed byte, 0 for non-buildable types) and a breeding-rate-shaped accumulator (`+0xA0`, incremented by a per-population-band amount and compared against a per-type threshold `0x5A7228+0x36`, the likely real source of the previously-noted "every 16 turns" AVERAGE cadence - an accumulating-probability roll, not a hard turn-count modulo; this session did not find an explicit `turn & 0xF` check anywhere in this function or its only confirmed caller). On a successful roll: queues a pending-handoff record on the global stack `0x892443` (the same convention used for spirits/pillars/patrol markers elsewhere in this catalog) and `alloc_unit`s a BRAND-NEW class-2 building object (the next size hut, confirming "creates the next size at 0x4051FE"), copying several fields from the old instance, then **seeds the NEW building's own wood-stock companion (resolved via its `+0x82` link) with a one-time, unconditional `0x4BA2C0(companion, +0x64)` (+100 wood, exactly one "wood piece") right after zeroing its stock** - every freshly-(re)created building instance (a size-up hut confirmed here) starts its 0-4 visual-construction-stage climb with one piece already free, matching `docs/specs/buildings.md`'s own "the first piece of wood is brought to the site... as in the game" line, except the exe grants it by fiat at creation rather than a brave fetching it. Only confirmed caller this session: `0x403582`, inside `0x403280`/`unit_processing_class_2_bldg` (own row) - called there UNCONDITIONALLY every turn, alongside several other per-type-flag-gated sibling calls (`0x4055F0`/`0x405B80`/`0x406600` depending on table `0x5A7270` bits) - so if "every 16 turns" is real, the periodicity is internal to this function's own accumulator, not an external modulo at the call site. **Open**: whether ordinary (non-hut, or non-growth/initial) building PLACEMENT reaches this SAME function/call site for its own free first wood piece, or a sibling one, was not confirmed this session.
See `0x4050C0`'s own row (this address is the `0x4BA2C0(companion,+100)` call site inside it, cited from `0x4BA2C0`'s own row's task-#12 addendum).

training_building_turn: cost, conversion (delete occupants, alloc new persons); also autonomously allocates and assigns kind-3 "go to a position" command groups (0x436c20/0x438730 flags=0x20/0x436d00) to up to a handful of its own occupants (word list at building+0x86 - the fixed 6-slot occupant array, see 0x407490's row; the earlier "capacity ~20" guess here was never grounded in a read value and is now superseded), target position from a per-building-type "zone" table (0x5a7228/0x5a7248 plus world-space table 0x59df3c, none decoded) - the only confirmed non-player, non-combat autonomous command-group assignment found so far; inferred (not proven) to be occupant/queue positioning (training slot or worship spot), not wood-related; kind 4 (the "doing it" half, handler 0x433800) not yet read. **Correction this session: 0x5a7259/0x5a707f, previously lumped into that "none decoded" zone table, are NOT position data at all - they're building_type[output]+0x31 (the "output person" byte, matching the Ghidra export's own `objs0`-family-adjacent `unit_type_person`/building-type struct recovery, cross-checked against pop3-rev-analysis.md's already-documented building-type-table row) and `unit_type_person[type]+0x1F` (`CONV_<type>`) respectively. Line-by-line traced this session (0x405BA0-0x405C8B) and confirmed exactly matches pop3-rev-analysis.md's already-solved training "Cost" section formula: walks the occupant word-list at building+0x86 up to building_type[output]+0x20 ("slots"), resolves each occupant via the global id table (0x890390), skips busy/invalid/already-output-type occupants (`occupant+0x2A`==0 or `occupant+0x2B`==building_type[output]+0x31), and accumulates `points += CONV_<occupant_type>` for the rest - i.e. this IS the `points = sum over occupants whose type != output of CONV_<type>` line, not a separate undecoded mechanic. No open question left here; the genuinely-undecoded "zone"/position table for the kind-3 move-order placement is elsewhere in this same function and still unidentified. **Resolved this session (task #9, "6 vs ~20" discrepancy)**: `building_type[output]` here is indexed by the TRAINING BUILDING'S OWN type byte (`+0x2b`), confirmed directly in the disassembly (0x405D12-0x405D1F: `type*0x4c + 0x5A7248`) - "output" is accurate in effect only because each training building type has exactly one output profession (that same type entry's own `+0x31` field), not a separately-indexed "output building type". The referenced `+0x20` "slots" value, read directly from the shipped exe for every real building type, is ALWAYS <= 6 (full per-type table in 0x407490's row) - it is a per-type OPERATIONAL cap on the SAME physical 6-slot array, never a larger array. The earlier "capacity ~20" guess was simply wrong and is now superseded; there is exactly one 6-slot occupant array at `+0x86`, shared by every building instance of every type.
adds a training building's stored mana to a type 1 tribe

**Vehicle hut's own per-turn operational handler (building state 2, types 13-16 only, dispatched via `unit_processing_class_2_bldg`/0x403280's own per-type-flag check, table 0x5A7228+0x48 bit 0x40) - traced this session chasing task #10 (the vehicle-hut wood-delivery rate).** Every call: clears a stale transient-marker reference (`+0x84`) if it no longer resolves live; if the hut has ANY occupant (`+0xA6`!=0), prunes its 6-slot crew array (`+0x86`, see `0x407490`'s row) counting idle (own `+0xA9`==0) vs busy crew, evicting any slot that no longer resolves to a live person (`0x407490`); if MORE than half the resolved crew is idle, picks ONE idle crew member and sets its own work sub-state to `+0xA8=0x1F` (31) plus a "committed" flag (`+0x76` bit 0x10) - **this is the per-turn recruitment throttle: only one additional idle crew member is sent out to fetch wood per turn, never the whole idle pool at once** (a second throttle at `+0x70>=0x50` inside the same block sends an already-partway-through-something crew member back out too, not fully disambiguated this session); if at least one crew member is actively working, the hut's own `+0xA4` word (the wood-delivery accumulator) is nonzero, and no transient marker is already pending (`+0x84`==0): spawns a class-6/type-7 marker at a per-type door-relative offset (table `0x59DF3C`, keyed by a footprint-shape byte from `0x895EC1`) and stores its id in `+0x84` (role not fully traced - plausibly a visual/placeholder object, not itself wood-related). **Separately, gated on a sited-clearance check (`0x4B9EF0`) at the computed spawn point: reads the hut's own TYPE's "output" byte (`unit_type_building[type]+0x31`, table base `0x5A7228`, confirmed 1:1 as the VEHICLE type - 13/14->1/2 boat, 15/16->3/4 balloon), looks up `vehicle_type_table[vehicletype]+0xB` (table base `0x5A7940`, stride 23 bytes/entry, confirmed raw from the exe: 600 for vehicle type 1/2 = boat hut 1/2, 1000 for type 3/4 = balloon hut 1/2) and compares the hut's own `+0xA4` against it: if `+0xA4` is still LESS than that threshold, does nothing further this turn; once `+0xA4 >= threshold`: zeroes `+0xA4` back to 0 and proceeds to actually create the vehicle (class 4, the mapped type, heading/position work continuing past 0x4069E5, reaching `alloc_unit`/`init_unit_class`/`init_unit_type_4` - 0x4ED5B0/0x4631B0, own rows - not re-traced in full this session) and clears the `+0x84` marker if one existed.** **`+0xA4` is confirmed as the hut's OWN wood-delivery accumulator, gated directly against this per-vehicle-type 600/1000 threshold - the only function found anywhere that INCREMENTS `+0xA4` is the generic transfer primitive `0x4A7860` (own row), called from a crew member's own "deliver wood" work state (`0x496750`, own row) - this function (0x406600) never writes a positive value into `+0xA4` itself, only reads/clears it.** Net: there is NO flat "+N wood per turn" constant anywhere in this function - production rate is driven by (a) how many crew slots the hut has (per-type cap already confirmed in `0x407490`'s row: 4 for either boat-hut type, 6 for either airship-hut type), (b) a one-new-worker-per-turn recruitment throttle when over half the resolved crew is idle, and (c) each recruited crew member's own independent chop/travel/deliver cycle time (see `0x496750`'s row) - the per-DELIVERY lump size and gating threshold are now exact, but the resulting real-world turns-per-vehicle figure depends on travel distance to a wood source and cannot be reduced to one static number from this function alone.

Vehicle hut (building types 13-16, per-type flag `0x5A7228`+0x48 bit `0x40`) per-turn production, `unit_processing_class_2_bldg`'s (`0x403280`) own state-2 branch for this type family. Traced this session (pop3-rev-analysis.md "Vehicle huts: how the hut itself produces a vehicle"). Confirms building type -> vehicle type is a clean 1:1 via `0x5A7228`+0x31 (13->1, 14->2, 15->3, 16->4). Crew: the generic `+0x86` occupant array (same field `0x407490`'s own row calls a "6-slot array"; this function hardcodes exactly 6 slots scanned too, consistent - but `0x405B80`'s own row describes a per-type loop bound up to ~20 on the SAME field for training buildings, an unresolved discrepancy between the two rows, not re-checked this session), bucketed into idle (own `+0xA9` clear) vs busy. `+0x84` is a transient class-6/type-7 marker object (own id, created once idle crew exists and `+0x84` is empty, deleted once the real vehicle spawns) - NOT a pilot/driver reference despite its position in the function. `+0xA4` (word) is the hut's own wood-delivery accumulator for the vehicle's `WOOD_VEHICLE_*` cost (vehicle-type table `0x5A7938`+0x13, already in pop3-rev-analysis.md's Vehicles table: 600 boat / 1000 balloon) - what increments it per turn was not located in this function. Once `+0xA4` reaches the cost: resets to 0, re-derives a per-type spawn point (door-relative offset through table `0x59DF3C`, decoded this session - previously "none decoded" per `0x405B80`'s own row), gated on a clearance check (`0x4B9EF0`, not independently traced), and calls `alloc_unit(class=4, mapped vehicle type, tribe, pos)`.

building state 3 finalize, entered once the foundation check (0x408080) has already set state=3: first, if a worker was inside (+0xa6, same slot `training_building_turn` 0x405b80 checks), evicts everyone (0x407490) one at a time. Then branches on sub-state (+0x2d, the same byte 0x408080 writes as 1 "uneven ground" or 2 "flooded") - confirming Ghidra's own name `alloc_spell_blast_or_sinking` is exactly right, and confirming the two foundation-check destroy reasons really are two different outcomes, not the same one twice: sub-state 1 shatters the building's own mesh into flying debris pieces (0x407860) then allocates a "simple blast" (class 7 type 1, same components as the Blast spell, same push constants 140/98) centred on it - a violent explosion, matching "too steep/uneven ground" as the visibly destructive reason; sub-state 2 instead hands the building off through the same pending-handoff LIFO slot (0x892443) person-death uses for its spirit controller (0x4d5cf0/0x502910) and allocates a class 10 type 0x13 object at its position (not independently confirmed, but by the slot it reuses and the sub-state's own meaning, plausibly a quiet "sinks beneath the water" visual) - matching flooding as a non-violent reason; any other sub-state value (not currently produced by 0x408080) skips both and goes straight to the shared cleanup. Shared cleanup regardless of sub-state (gated on +0x14 bit 0x40, skipped if set): calls 0x403860(self) then, if +0xaf != 0xff, decrements a per-tribe stat via 0x41b550; finally always calls 0x4edcf0(self) - the generic "remove this thing" teardown. No ashes are made on this path (0x40B230 is never called here) - ashes come from the separate attack/fire-destruction route (0x4092A0).
enter_building(person, building): slot, training flag, cost

`fn(building, specific_occupant_or_null) -> void`, traced this session (previously only referenced by role - "evicts everyone"/"evicts each occupant" - in several other rows, e.g. `0x406F40`, insect plague `0x510120`, never itself opened). Finds the occupant slot in the building's own 6-slot array (`+0x86`): the SPECIFIC one passed in if given (matched by its own cell-index field `+0x24`), else the FIRST occupied slot. Removes them: decrements the building's own occupancy count (`+0xA6`), clears that slot, clears a bit in `+0x9C`, and re-inserts the evicted person onto the land tile at the building's own position via `0x4D80E0` (`insert_unit_into_land_tile`, already cited in person_states.tsv row 5).
